newsitem.title: USA: Greenberg agrees to buy J.M. Specialties.
newsitem.headline: Greenberg agrees to buy J.M. Specialties.

text.p: William Greenberg Jr. Desserts and Cafes Inc said on Friday that it agreed in principle to buy J.M. Specialties Inc for about $3 million in cash and stock.
The New Jersey-based J.M. Specialties makes, sells and distributes batter and frozen finished cakes, brownies and muffins under the Batter Bake name.
William Greenberg said J.M. Specialties founder Philip Grabow would be chief executive officer of the combined companies. The deal was expected to be completed within 60 days, it said.
The company also said it planned to change its name to more accurately reflect the range of its combined businesses.
William Greenberg, Jr. offers pastries, cakes, pies, cookies and other desserts and sells them in its own stores as well as through its wholesale division.

The company said Stephen Fass would continue as president of William Greenberg Jr. and Maria Marfuggi would become president of J.M. Specialities, with overall responsibility for wholesale operations.
J.M. Specialties had sales of about $3.6 million for the fiscal year ended December 31, 1995 and net income of about $113,000, William Greenberg Jr said.
